newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wiluna says finds new gold ore body.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wiluna says finds new gold ore body.

text.p: Western Australian gold miner Wiluna Mines Ltd said on Tuesday it had found a significant new body of gold ore south of its Bulletin mine at Wiluna.
Wiluna said a series of thick ore grade intersections had been recorded in diamond drill holes south of the Bulletin Mine.

"The widely spaced drill holes indicated the presence of significant zones of mineralisation of comparable grade and thickness to the Bulletin orebody that is currently being developed and is producing at an annualised rate of over 100,000 ounces," Wiluna said.
Drilling in the December quarter had found two major mineralised zones which had been named the Woodley Lode and the Lennon Lode, it said.
The two lodes would be readily accesible by extensions to the current Bulletin decline, Wiluna said.
Wiluna Managing Director Jeff Gresham said it was an important discovery for the company now that its expanded BIOX plant was operating close to design capacity and could be used to process new ore.

"New ore sources that can be assessed from existing mine development will have a significant positive impact on the cost structure and potential levels of production of the operation," Gresham said in a statement.
Follow-up infill and extensional drilling would be carried out during the March Quarter with drilling planned to recommence in mid-January.
Ore grades reported by Wiluna included one intersection of 1.0 metre of ore grading 127.00 grams per tonne (g/t) gold in the Lennon Lode.
Other intersections in the same lode ranged from 4.27 g/t over 5.4 metres to 16.82 g/t over 4.7 metres.
In the Woodley orebody, grades ranged from 2.34 g/t over 3.6 metres to 9.27 g/t over 15.4 metres.
Wiluna's share price was up one cent at 89 cents at 1.05 p.m. (0205 GMT).
